survey: A beach ball rests on rippled sand, seen from slightly above and a little to the front-left. The ball is a sphere made of six gores (red, white, green, white, blue, white) that meet at a purple cap. The cap sits on the upper-left front of the sphere, a little off the centre of the silhouette. Because the cap is only slightly turned away from the camera, it is drawn as a near-circular, very slightly flattened disc. It has a thin visible edge on its lower side, which matches a top-down view. All gore seams start at the cap and curve down and to the right over the sphere, toward a hidden opposite pole at the lower back. They narrow and bunch up as the surface turns away, which is correct. The sand is seen from above at the same moderate angle: its ripples flatten into horizontal bands toward the top of the frame. The ball sits into the sand with a soft contact shadow underneath, falling to the lower left. The ball, its cap, its seams and the ground all agree on one camera.
